accuracy.evidence: Checked 610 against NC Year 4 ('recognise the place value of each digit in a four-digit number') and CCSS 4.NBT.1/4.NBT.2. Every worked number re-done by hand: 3,452 = 3 Th 4 H 5 T 2 O; 5,555 = 5000+500+50+5; 3,052 vs 352; 2 Th + 13 H + 4 T + 6 O = 3,346 = 3 Th 3 H 4 T 6 O after exchange; 80+6000+9+700 = 6,789; 8,305 = 8000+300+5; ordering 3,099 < 3,190 < 3,901 < 9,013.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented place-value slips: giving the face value instead of the value (the 7 in 7,345 'is 7'), dropping a zero that holds a place (5 thousands 7 ones written 57; 3,052 built as 352, which the lab names), writing jumbled expanded parts in the order given (8,697), and leaving 13 counters in one place rather than exchanging ten 100s for a 1000.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagpvc uses place value counters (discs worth 1000/100/10/1) on a four-column Th-H-T-O chart with a ten-for-one exchange into the thousands and a jumbled-parts sort; flag3digit uses base-ten flats/rods for three digits, flagplace shifts digits for x10/÷10, flagtenten swaps 10 tens for a hundred. Lab gate measured under 30% shingle overlap with all flag_*.js.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner sees the digit at the top change only from counters in its own column, finds the value of each 5 by tapping (the column shows '= 500'), discovers that an empty column still prints 0, makes 13 hundreds collapse to 1 thousand + 3 hundreds with the total unchanged, and builds 6,789 from parts dropped by place.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: '400' (value, not count) for the 100 counters in 3,452; 'they are all just 5' for 5,555; 'zero is worth nothing, leave it out' for 3,052; '13 thousands' for 13 hundreds; '8,697' (parts in written order) for 80+6000+9+700.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Generated questions alternate between 'what is the d in N worth?' and 'which number is a000 + c0 + d?'. Each wrong option has its own message: face value ('that is just the digit'), one place off ('one place too far left'), missing zero ('write 0 to hold that place'), tens and ones swapped. Wrong-column drops in the lab name the counter's own column.

readability.evidence: Kid text reads at FK grade 0.4 and adult at 5.8 (family targets 5.0 and 10.0). Short sentences and the exact Year 4 terms: digit, place, place value, thousands/hundreds/tens/ones, expanded form, zero holding a place, exchange.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate found no filler phrases. Each kid paragraph states one rule with an example (places, value, ten times, zero holding a place); adult paragraphs give the standard, the digit × place rule, four named mistakes and what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at iPhone 13 (dark) and 360 px Android (light) for all 7 steps: four columns fit with 13 counters stacked in the hundreds, digit boxes 28 px, counters labelled 1000/100/10/1, part cards and young-size 56 px buttons reachable; nothing clipped.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has a button twin (+/− for each counter, Th/H/T/O 5 reveal, 'Swap ten 100s for one 1000', Pick part then Put in column); the canvas aria-label is updated with each message; walk.cjs axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.

sources: Department for Education, National Curriculum in England: mathematics programmes of study, Year 4 number and place value ('recognise the place value of each digit in a four-digit number (thousands, hundreds, tens, and ones)')

CCSS Math 4.NBT.1 (a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right) and 4.NBT.2 (read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names and expanded form)
